inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report note 24 cash-flow reconciliation, share-based payments $2.368m (thousands in filing); no cash tax on equity-award settlement disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 across history)
inputs.share_count_basis: Adjusted weighted average shares for diluted EPS, FY2026 Annual Report note 6: 1,247,450,463 (1,246,006,654 on issue + ~1.4m performance rights). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The 10%/~$900.9m on-market buyback authorised Nov-2025 to 23-Nov-2026 has bought NOTHING -- shares on issue were 1,246,006,654 at both 30-Jun-2025 and 30-Jun-2026 and ShareRepurchases is 0 in every period since FY2015. Authorised is not spent; buyback_cash recorded as 0.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD build: AU 10-year government bond ~4.5% (Sept 2026, after three RBA increases in 2026), ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.1 for rate-sensitive big-ticket discretionary retail -> cost of equity ~10.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6% on the syndicated facility (bank interest $55.3m on ~$1.09bn average borrowings), ~4.2% after 30% tax. Weights ~85/15 on equity/ex-lease net debt (market cap ~$5.25bn, net debt $0.94bn) -> WACC ~9.5%. One WACC across all three scenarios; cyclicality, the UK losses and the regulatory overhang are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full FY26 lease cash of $226.3m (principal $156.6m in financing + interest on lease liabilities $69.6m in operating) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (5.3% of FY26 revenue, 5.4% FY25), and the $1,346.2m of lease liabilities is EXCLUDED from net debt (total_debt = borrowings only, $1,239.5m). To avoid charging leases twice, EBITDA is stated BEFORE the AASB16 non-cash charges: the $83.1m fair-value remeasurement of leasehold investment-property right-of-use assets is added back, and D&A is ex right-of-use depreciation ($102.9m = $181.9m total less $79.0m ROU depreciation).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is small (FY26 profit attributable to NCI $8.6m, 1.6% of PAT; NCI equity $43.0m). Charged once, in the bridge: -$43.0m carrying value deducted; flows are left whole-group.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing row: operating company, non-US, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). Harvey Norman is an integrated franchisor / company-operated retailer / large-format-retail landlord; the ~$4.8bn freehold property book ($4,191.7m investment property + $596.8m owner-occupied at 30-Jun-2026) is occupied mainly by its own franchisees, so its value is inseparable from the franchise network that pays the rent. A sum-of-parts or NAV component was considered and rejected: (1) the property's cash return -- $321.8m rent and outgoings from franchisees plus $144.2m from external tenants -- is already inside the consolidated flows, so capitalising the property separately and valuing the franchising segment on earnings that are net of that rent would require an intra-group rent strip the segment note does not support cleanly; (2) the only property-specific income NOT in the flows is the non-cash revaluation gain, which is a mark, not a cash stream. The house treatment is therefore: rent in the flows, revaluation gains OUT of the flows, property capex charged in full, and NTA reported as an asset-backing reference in valuation_philosophy rather than added to the bridge. EBITDA BASE: the DB's EBITDA (PBT + finance costs + D&A = $1,098.9m FY26) includes $170.7m of non-cash fair-value gains ($154.9m Australian freehold investment property, $1.9m overseas property, $13.9m equity investments), $14.2m interest income, the $83.1m AASB16 leasehold-ROU remeasurement expense and the $18.8m one-off ASIC pecuniary penalty. Clean pre-lease EBITDA = 1,098.9 + 83.1 - 170.7 - 14.2 + 18.8 = $1,015.8m = 23.8% of the $4,266.4m revenue base (23.4% FY25, 22.5% FY24, 25.2% FY23 on the same construction). JV share of profit ($19.6m) is kept in EBITDA because it is cash-backed (distributions received $18.9m). REVENUE BASE is product sales + revenues from franchisees ($3,051.8m + $1,214.6m); external rent, interest and other income sit in 'Revenues and other income items' and flow through the margin rather than the revenue line. Interest income is stripped (its asset, cash, is in net debt). Listed equity investments are added to the bridge at fair value because their revaluation was stripped from EBITDA. Buyback: none executed (see share_count_basis); the flat count is a modelling convention the company is funding through a 0.06%-of-revenue SBC charge, which is effectively an SBC-zero market -- house and street bases nearly coincide.
inputs.fy0_component_check: FY26 rebuilt from the drivers: EBITDA 1,015.8 - lease 226.3 - SBC 2.4 - D&A 102.9 = EBIT 684.3 vs the company's own PBT ex-AASB16/ex-revaluations/ex-penalty of $654.7m plus bank interest $57.1m less interest income $14.2m = $697.6m (1.9% apart; the residual is the AASB16 timing difference and other-income noise). Unlevered owner FCF at FY26 drivers ~ $302m; after after-tax bank interest ~$261m, against actual levered post-lease owner FCF of $80m in FY26 (GST timing -$106m, JV loans -$21m, working capital) and $250m in FY25.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_3yr_cagr (3.4%) tempered downward: retained revaluation gains inflate equity growth, and the 7-year revenue CAGR of 4.3% (FY19-26) spans the COVID demand surge. 3.0% is the base-case mid-path growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR 3.4% vs EPS 3-yr CAGR -0.6% and revenue 5-yr CAGR 0.7%: divergence >30%. The 5-year series start at the FY2021 COVID peak (EPS 67.4c, PBT $1.18bn), which depresses every 5-year rate; the 3-year rates from FY2023 are the better read of the current cycle. Equity compounding is partly retained non-cash revaluation gains.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income; SBC is <0.2% of FCF so the owner and reported series move together). The FY26 endpoint is depressed by a $106m adverse GST-payment timing swing and $21m of loans to JV entities; FY25 owner FCF was $409m on the same basis. Revenue growth FY17->FY18 is understated by a franchise-revenue accounting basis change (FY15-17 on the old note-3 basis, ~$75m/yr higher than the FY19 restatement).

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +1.5%: July-2026 aggregated sales were -3.4% (Australian franchisees) and -4.4% (NZ) against a 6.4%/7.2% comparative, offset by August written sales +3.8%, rent indexation ~3% and one new complex plus three freehold relocations; management said momentum 'moderated' in 2H26 with three RBA increases. FY28-31 3.0-3.5% as the rate cycle turns and the AI device replacement cycle, Croatia flagship (2028) and UK stores add; tapering to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-lease clean EBITDA margin 23.8% FY26 was flattered by a strong 1H (franchising PBT +14.2%) and dented in 2H (franchising -15.1%); opex/system sales rose to 18.7%. FY27 23.3% (softer sales, UK losses -$31m continuing, inflation in freight/energy), recovering to the 24.0% mid-cycle level by FY30. FY23-26 range on the same construction was 22.5-25.2%.
base.capex_rationale: FY26 capex 6.6% of revenue (PPE+intangibles $150.5m, freehold investment property $133.2m); 5-year average 6.8%. Tapered to 5.0% by FY34 as the property acquisition programme normalises toward growth-consistent reinvestment (~2.5% growth on ~$5.8bn of property and PPE plus maintenance ~D&A). Property capex is charged in full even though it builds an appreciating asset whose revaluation gains are excluded -- deliberately conservative, see valuation_philosophy.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid $185.8m on PBT ex-revaluations of $619.6m = 30.0% in FY26; statutory 30% Australia with lower rates on Singapore/Ireland/Malaysia/NZ earnings. 29.5% on unlevered EBIT.
base.wc_rationale: Overseas company-operated retail carries inventory and the franchisor carries franchisee receivables; growth consumes ~5% of the revenue increase.

scenario_narratives.base: The rate cycle stalls the big-ticket consumer for one more year (FY27 revenue +1.5%: July-2026 Australian franchisee sales -3.4%, NZ -4.4%, Singapore -5.4%) before housing turnover and the AI-device replacement cycle (Copilot+ PCs, AI mobiles) restore 3-3.5% growth from FY28. Clean pre-lease EBITDA margin dips to 23.3% on inflation in freight/energy and a widening UK loss, then recovers to the 24.0% mid-cycle level. Property capex stays elevated near-term (one new complex, three freehold relocations, East Zagreb land) then tapers to 5% of revenue. Rent from franchisees and external tenants (~$466m) is the property portfolio's contribution to value; the ~$155m/yr of revaluation gains are excluded as non-cash marks.
scenario_narratives.bull: Consumer confidence recovers faster as the RBA pauses; the AI device cycle and technology categories carry Australian franchisee sales to +3.5% in FY27 and 5% in FY28-29; Established International (NZ, Ireland, Singapore/Malaysia, Slovenia/Croatia, +25.2% PBT in FY26) keeps compounding and the UK reaches breakeven by FY29 as the West Midlands cluster fills out. Margin expands to 25.0% (the FY23 level was 25.2%), tax edges lower on the overseas mix, and the terminal cap is 15x. Even in this case the company does not execute the authorised buyback.
scenario_narratives.bear: Higher-for-longer rates and a soft housing market cut Australian franchisee sales for two years (-2%, 0%): franchising PBT, which fell 15.1% in 2H26, keeps falling and franchisee financial-accommodation losses rise; the UK loss widens rather than closes; Amazon/JB Hi-Fi/Temu take share from a weaker online proposition; the ASIC adverse-publicity order blunts promotional-finance campaigns. Margin troughs at 21.5% (below the FY24 trough of 22.5%), lease cost creeps to 5.6% of revenue as sales deleverage, and the terminal cap is 12x. No solvency risk: net debt/equity 18.8% with $4.8bn of freehold property; the bear case is an earnings and multiple case, not a balance-sheet case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the business is one of the most rate-sensitive on the ASX, 2H26 franchising PBT was already down 15.1%, July-2026 trading was negative in four of seven markets, and the UK loss is widening. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs a consumer recovery, a sustained AI device cycle AND a UK breakeven together. No going-concern or covenant risk (net debt/equity 18.8%, $4.8bn freehold property) so bear is not pushed higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF on an unlevered, ex-lease, ex-revaluation basis. The consolidated EBITDA is cleaned of $170.7m of non-cash fair-value gains, $14.2m interest income and the $18.8m one-off ASIC penalty, and restated pre-AASB16 so that the full $226m lease cash can be charged once inside EBIT with lease liabilities kept out of net debt. Property is valued through the rent it earns (in the flows) and charged for the capex it consumes; the ~$155m/yr of revaluation gains are treated as marks, not cash. This is deliberately harsher than the market's usual lens for HVN (price ~1.1x NTA of $3.79/share basic, $4.37 including right-of-use assets), because appreciation on large-format retail property is a cap-rate bet the cash flows do not have to fund. A reader who believes the property book is worth its independent valuations should read the NTA as the asset-backing floor and the house DCF as what the operating cash flows alone support; the gap between the two is the price of the property thesis.
valuation_philosophy.asset_backing_reference: Net tangible assets $4,717m at 30-Jun-2026 (FY26 AR p.4-5) = $3.79/share on 1,246.0m shares; freehold investment property $4,191.7m and owner-occupied land and buildings $596.8m at independent/directors' valuation. Not added to the bridge: the rent those assets earn is already in the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Consumer discretionary and interest-rate sensitivity: a further RBA move or housing-turnover slump pushes FY27-28 toward the bear path (July-2026 Australian franchisee sales -3.4%).
Revaluation dependence in reported earnings: $156.75m of the $790.3m FY26 PBT is a non-cash property mark; cap-rate expansion would hit reported EPS and NTA even though this model excludes it.
UK expansion loss (-$31.2m FY26, +33.5% YoY) with no stated breakeven; the bear case assumes it widens.

Property capex charged in full (6.5% of revenue tapering to 5%) while revaluation gains are excluded: if property spend continues at the FY23-26 pace without tapering, value is ~$0.30-0.40/share lower; if it stops, higher.
The 10% buyback authorisation ($900.9m) has never been executed; value is not credited for it, and a genuine execution at current prices would be accretive to the per-share figures here.
Regulatory: $35m Federal Court penalty and adverse-publicity order over interest-free finance advertising; promotional credit is a historically important sales driver.
GST/working-capital timing: FY26 OCF fell $157m on a $106m GST-payment swing; the model normalises this, so a structural rise in working capital would lower the flows.
